headline: Seattle Pacific finish their conference season and wait
dek: Seattle Pacific closed their conference schedule by beating Northwest Nazarene and sit top of the table. Western Oregon, who won at Simon Fraser the same day, go to Western Washington on Saturday needing a win, because a draw would not be enough.
displaced_by: Seattle Pacific have played their last conference match and Western Oregon won at Simon Fraser, so the standing dek's remaining-matches sentence is no longer true.

pattern.label: derived
pattern.text: Saint Martin's 32 goals are more than Simon Fraser, Western Washington or Northwest Nazarene have scored, yet they sit bottom of the table: most of their goals have come against sides outside the conference, not in the matches the table counts.

wire.line: Western Oregon must win at Western Washington to overtake Seattle Pacific for the title.

findings.label: observed
findings.text: Three matches whose dates have passed carry no result, and every one of them is a Simon Fraser home match from August.

findings.label: derived
findings.text: Seattle Pacific have won fourteen matches, more than any other programme in the conference.

findings.label: observed
findings.text: Archie Dhima has 16 goals from 53 shots for Western Oregon.

findings.label: observed
findings.text: Elijah Brockl has kept seven shutouts for Northwest Nazarene.

findings.label: observed
findings.text: Of the shots on target Austin Valdez has faced for Western Oregon, 78 were saved and 21 went in.

last_match.line: Western Oregon have won every match since their goalless draw at Northwest Nazarene.

next_match.line: Western Oregon won the September meeting between the two at home.

validation.policy: observed and derived claims are recomputed against the data home before publish; failures are dropped, not softened. signal and projected pass on schema unless the data contradicts a figure. context is never validated as a finding.
